description: `is_a?`'s type argument evaluates to a word that is not a recognized Core type, raising `ol-unknown-type` naming the word — the same code and params as the worded form's rule (`spec/commands.md:708`, `spec/error-model.md:127`). Issue #99. WHY stage=runtime, when `spec/error-model.md:127` registers `ol-unknown-type` as `semantic`: the PREFIX form evaluates its type argument (`spec/execution-model.md:167-169`, `spec/grammar.md:234`), so in general the type word is a computed value the checker cannot know. The WORDED form `is a` instead takes a literal type word in the grammar, and is caught at the registered stage — measured, `check()` over `print (5 is a "banana")` reports `ol-unknown-type`/`semantic`, while `check()` over this fixture's program reports nothing at all. Note what is NOT claimed: this fixture's own type argument is a literal, so it is statically knowable, and `spec/tooling.md:197-200` says a semantic tool SHOULD report statically knowable uses of runtime codes. The measured fact is only that THIS implementation's checker does not fold prefix-call arguments, so the fault reaches the runtime guard; a checker that reported the literal case would also conform. The sibling pair pins both sides: `core-language/check/type-unknown-in-is-a` and `core-language/execution/is-a-unknown-type`. That reason is independent of issue #815: this fixture's events and diagnostics are identical before and after it — measured at `2a1888c1`, the saga base predating #815, and at this commit. Since #815 `execute()` DOES run Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:632`, `:659-664`); here the check finds nothing, so Phase 2 begins, and execution halts at the failing statement keeping the `instruction` event asserted below. Issue #1156 corrected two false claims this description previously carried: that the stage was runtime because `execute()` did not run the checker — which #815 falsified — and a denial that this statement executed at all, which contradicted the event asserted below and was pasted from the check-caught sibling `is-a-unknown-type`, where both of its clauses are measured true.
